# s273 — Link a sliver to its parent slice with a parent field

An item gains an optional `parent` field naming the slice it is a sliver of. A sliver is a small child item (size S, effort 1) that a relay orchestrator carves out of a larger slice so a cheaper implementer can take it. This slice adds the link and the views; s274 adds the readiness and finish rules, and s275 the relay guidance.

**Findings:** owner request, session 2026-10-14: slivers (parent:child) for relays · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — Ready for review, gate PASS. Item.parent added at index schema 9 (historical items load empty without writes; the repo's own index was stamped to 9 through a no-op 'set s273 --effort 2', which left one set entry in the log). add, set and list take --parent (set --parent '' clears it); show lists slivers in text and JSON (slivers key, dropped by --lean when empty); remove and purge refuse an item that still has slivers unless forced, and a purged parent's id is not reclaimed while a sliver names it. Outline parent: resolves like depends: (orchestrator decision): a known title wins (an entry in the outline or an existing item, full or short title), otherwise the value must be an existing item ID; one level, self and unknown checks are refused before any write. Stable codes parent_self and parent_nested (unknown parent is no_such_item); verify and the index merge driver report unknown, nested and self parents (messages only, no code field on findings). **Not in this slice:**

## Why

The owner asked on 2026-10-14 for slivers to be tracked items with a parent:child relationship, one level deep. Today the only item-to-item links are `depends_on` and `discovered_from`; neither says "this is part of that". s258's split parts are untracked, so a sliver's status, notes and attempts have nowhere to live.

## Boundary

- One level only: an item with a parent cannot itself be a parent, and an item cannot be its own parent.
- `parent` is a reference, not a dependency. Readiness and finish rules belong to s274; this slice does not change `next`, `handoff` or `done`.
- Follow the `discovered_from` pattern from s210 (commit 07c37ef) everywhere it applies. No new mechanism where that one fits.
